node_definition.done_when: Read section 25 of crew-runtime-positive-controls first. First show the defect still reproduces at your base. Dispatch two nodes on one plan in a temporary config home: both are granted the plan HTML, its cumulative evidence record and its figures directory, and the second dispatch's live_conflicts reads empty. Then a dispatch whose granted paths collide with a live pointer's claims reports them in live_conflicts and in conflicts, naming both runs and the shared paths. A dispatch whose caller-named paths collide behaves exactly as it does today. A path granted to a run that has since been promoted is not reported, because a released claim is not a conflict. Reporting is the change asked for here; whether a granted collision also refuses the dispatch stays as it is today. The code is the live-claim conflict check in reckon/crew/dispatch.py. tests/test_granted_path_is_a_claim.py carries three cases, a granted collision, a caller-named collision and a promoted holder, and the first fails at your base. Existing tests reaching live_conflicts, the scope check and dry-run dispatch keep passing; grep tests/ for live_conflicts, conflicts, claim_map and granted to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/granted-path-is-a-claim.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
